description: A mathematically-inclined junior who has primarily used high-level languages like Python and Java and is now tackling systems-level concepts for the first time.

nodes.title: C Programming Primer for Systems
nodes.personalizationRationale: This student has no_prior_exposure to systems programming, so a dedicated C-language primer is necessary to handle the course's programming assignments.
nodes.description: A foundational introduction to C syntax, pointers, and memory management specifically tailored for students with no prior experience in systems programming.

nodes.personalizationRationale: Because the student is in the no_prior_exposure tier, additional background on hardware-software interaction is required before diving into OS services.
nodes.description: Exploration of how the CPU, registers, and memory hierarchy interact with the operating system at a low level.
nodes.title: Hardware Foundations for OS
User vs. Kernel Mode Deep Dive
nodes.description: Detailed breakdown of the transition between user mode and kernel mode, including the role of system calls and interrupts.
nodes.personalizationRationale: For a student with no_prior_exposure, the concept of dual-mode operation requires extra scaffolding to ensure architectural understanding.

nodes.description: Overview of operating system services, structures (monolithic, microkernel, layered), and classic design concepts.
nodes.personalizationRationale: This core node ensures the no_prior_exposure student masters the standard syllabus definitions of OS services and structures.
nodes.title: OS Foundations & Structures
Process Concepts & Lifecycle
nodes.description: The process abstraction, including process control blocks (PCBs), state transitions, and context switching.
nodes.personalizationRationale: The process lifecycle is a foundational core concept that the no_prior_exposure student must master for all subsequent blocks.

nodes.title: Inter-Process Communication (IPC)
nodes.description: Mechanisms for processes to communicate, including shared memory and message passing systems.
nodes.personalizationRationale: This core topic introduces the complexities of communication between independent processes, essential for the no_prior_exposure student.

nodes.title: Threads & Threading Models
nodes.personalizationRationale: Understanding the distinction between processes and threads is a required core competency for students at the no_prior_exposure level.
nodes.description: Multithreading models (Many-to-One, One-to-One, Many-to-Many) and the Pthreads library.

nodes.personalizationRationale: Algorithmic evaluation is a core requirement; this node helps the no_prior_exposure student model system performance analytically.
nodes.description: Evaluation criteria for scheduling and analysis of algorithms like FCFS, SJF, Round Robin, and Priority Scheduling.
nodes.title: CPU Scheduling Algorithms

nodes.personalizationRationale: A mandatory assessment checkpoint to ensure the no_prior_exposure student is prepared for the week-8 midterm exam.
nodes.description: Comprehensive review of Chapters 1-5 material, including process management, threads, and scheduling in preparation for the midterm.
nodes.title: Midterm Review: Ch. 1-5
Critical Sections & Mutexes
nodes.personalizationRationale: Synchronization is a difficult topic; this core node provides the theoretical tools needed by the no_prior_exposure student for project deliveries.
nodes.description: Defining the critical section problem and the use of Mutex locks and Semaphores to ensure mutual exclusion.

nodes.title: Classic Problems of Synchronization
nodes.description: Solving classic problems such as Bounded-Buffer, Readers-Writers, and the Dining Philosophers using monitors and semaphores.
nodes.personalizationRationale: Applying synchronization primitives to classic problems is a core skill that the no_prior_exposure student will use in programming projects.

nodes.title: Deadlock Prevention & Avoidance
nodes.description: Deadlock characterization (the four conditions) and strategies for prevention, avoidance (Banker's Algorithm), and detection.
nodes.personalizationRationale: This core block is essential for the student to understand resource allocation failures and is tested on the final exam.

nodes.description: Memory allocation strategies, paging, and the structure of page tables.
nodes.personalizationRationale: Memory management is a core syllabus requirement; this node builds upon the hardware basics introduced earlier for the no_prior_exposure student.
nodes.title: Main Memory & Paging

nodes.description: Demand paging, page replacement algorithms (FIFO, LRU, Optimal), and the concept of thrashing.
nodes.personalizationRationale: Virtual memory is heavily project-relevant; the no_prior_exposure student must master these design tradeoffs.
nodes.title: Virtual Memory & Page Replacement
I/O Systems & File Storage
nodes.description: I/O hardware interfaces, performance subsystems, and the implementation of file systems on storage media.
nodes.personalizationRationale: This final core block covers the I/O and file-system concepts required for the cumulative final exam.

nodes.title: Final Review (Cumulative)
nodes.personalizationRationale: A final assessment checkpoint to consolidate learning across all blocks for the no_prior_exposure student prior to the cumulative final.
nodes.description: Cumulative review of the entire syllabus, focusing on design tradeoffs and practical applications for the final exam.
